decisions.decision: The hole, re-measured at bcca4a0 rather than taken from V2-084's escalation. (a) domain.RequirementPause occurs in exactly TWO non-test lines in the whole repository -- its declaration at internal/domain/model.go:444 and its switch case at model.go:510 -- and domain.RequirementCancel in exactly two, model.go:445 and model.go:515 (measured: `grep -rn '\bRequirementPause\b' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go | wc -l` returns 2, likewise for RequirementCancel). Nothing outside internal/domain ever constructs either command, so a Requirement cannot be paused and cannot be cancelled by any caller. (b) domain.RequirementResume does not exist at all: the same grep returns 0, and RequirementCommandKind (model.go:434-446) declares exactly nine kinds. (c) domain.Requirement (model.go:178-214) carries exactly SEVEN fields -- ID, Status, Version, Increments, StableSnapshot, RequestedBy, CapturedAt -- pinned name-by-name and in order by TestRequirementFieldListAndCaptureTagArePinned's want list at internal/domain/capture_time_test.go:250, and none of them can hold a previous status. (d) The pause branch at model.go:510-514 is admitted from exactly {ready, active, waiting, recovering} and sets paused; the cancel branch at model.go:515-519 is admitted from every status EXCEPT completed and cancelled. So the domain already models the entrance to paused and one of its two exits, and models neither the memory nor the other exit. This task adds the memory and the missing exit, and issues all three verbs.
decisions.rationale: The load-bearing observation in the outcome is that a paused state with no exit destroys a Requirement irrecoverably through what looks like a reversible action, so 'the way out' cannot be a follow-up. Measured, that danger is exact rather than rhetorical: today a paused Requirement's ONLY legal outgoing edge is cancel (measured -- paused appears as a source status in exactly one existing branch, the cancel branch, and in no other), so an application-level pause shipped alone would give the owner a button whose only sequel is destroying the Requirement. V2-084's A13(i) reached the same conclusion and stopped there because internal/domain was closed to it. internal/domain is open to this task, and that is the whole reason this task exists.

decisions.decision: The memory is ONE new field on domain.Requirement, PausedFrom RequirementStatus, and resume restores it verbatim. domain.RequirementResume is added as the tenth RequirementCommandKind, admitted from RequirementPaused ONLY, and it sets next.Status = current.PausedFrom and next.PausedFrom = "". The pause branch additionally sets next.PausedFrom = current.Status. Neither branch's admitted source set changes. The pausable set is declared ONCE, as a single unexported helper in model.go, and read twice: the pause branch's allowed(...) call and the resume branch's guard that current.PausedFrom is a member of it. Deriving resume's legal targets from pause's legal sources -- rather than declaring them a second time -- is what makes the round trip a structural property instead of two lists that can drift. The field carries NO struct tag, because TestRequirementFieldListAndCaptureTagArePinned (capture_time_test.go:283-285) fails if any field on this struct carries one and the Firestore adapter serializes the whole value with a plain json.Marshal (internal/store/firestore/store.go:210 and :266), so the persisted key is the Go field name.
decisions.rationale: The alternative that a hurried implementer will reach for is to widen the four existing branches so that ready, start, wait and recover each also admit paused. It was measured and it is the exact defect non_goals item 3 names: four widened branches let a resume land in ANY of the four statuses regardless of which one the Requirement was actually in, because nothing in the aggregate remembers. One new command that reads one field is strictly narrower than four widened branches, and the narrowness is measurable -- see d6's edge count. The second alternative, recovering the previous status by replaying the event stream, was rejected because internal/application has no port that reads events by aggregate inside a transaction, because two concurrent pauses could not be reasoned about, and because domain.Validate could then say nothing at all about the pair (status, resume target), which is where the guarantee has to live.

decisions.decision: Every edge this task adds is already described by the product, and this task adds ZERO product text. docs/** is prohibited entirely, and that is the answer to non_goals item 1 rather than a scope note. The citations, measured at bcca4a0 by reading the files: docs/architecture/domain-model.md:265 lists `paused` among ready's transition targets; :266 among active's; :267 among waiting's; :270 among recovering's -- exactly the four sources model.go:511 already admits, so the pause entrance agrees with the product in all four cells and in no more. domain-model.md:269 is the whole design of the exit: `| paused | 人間が処理を停止 | 直前の安全な非終端状態、cancelled |` -- the immediately preceding safe non-terminal state, and cancelled. That is two exits and it names the first one as a MEMORY of where the Requirement came from, not as a fixed status. docs/product/user-facing-spec.md:201, under section 4.8 'ループを制御する' whose subject is 利用者, lists 'Requirementのpause、resume、cancel' as one owner-issued triple. docs/product/definition.md:146 defines resume and :147 defines cancel requirement. user-facing-spec.md:274 and :277 define the two statuses in user-facing terms. domain-model.md:211 names pause, cancel and resume as Control Intent verbs 人間が発行した. The implementer must re-read every one of these and cite file, line and quoted text for every edge; an edge whose citation cannot be produced is the defect, and the correct response is to stop, not to add the edge with a weaker justification.
decisions.rationale: Requiring a citation per edge is only a real constraint if the citation set is closed and the edges are enumerable, and here both are. The product describes the entrance in exactly four cells and the exit in exactly one sentence, and this design adds exactly four pause edges (already present), one resume edge and zero cancel edges. Because the documents already say everything, an implementer who finds themselves editing docs/ to justify an edge has discovered that the edge is not described -- which is why docs/** is prohibited rather than merely unused: the prohibition converts non_goals item 1 from a promise into a build failure.

decisions.decision: The disagreement between the domain's cancel branch and the product's transition table, measured, recorded, and deliberately NOT repaired. domain-model.md:270 lists recovering's targets as active, waiting, needs-input, paused -- cancelled is NOT among them -- and :271 lists evaluating's as completed, active, needs-input -- cancelled is NOT among them. But model.go:515-519 admits cancel from every status except completed and cancelled, so it admits recovering and evaluating: the domain is WIDER than the table by exactly two cells. This task does not narrow the domain and does not narrow the application command either. The licence for the two extra cells is cited from a different altitude of the same product: definition.md:147 describes cancel requirement unconditionally as '指定したRequirementの以後の処理を止める' with no source-status qualifier; definition.md:132 requires the loop to '利用者の停止指示へ確実に従い'; definition.md:137 states '自律性は利用者の統制より優先されない'; and domain-model.md:336's effective-policy ladder places cancelled above graceful-stop and paused. A cancel that refused a Requirement stuck in recovering would be a stop the owner cannot issue in the one state where a stop is most likely to be wanted. The two-cell gap between the table and the branch is recorded as a named finding for the tech_lead and asserted nowhere.
decisions.rationale: This is the sharpest test of non_goals item 1 in the whole task and answering it by narrowing would have been the wrong reflex. Narrowing internal/domain's cancel branch would move TestInvariant3RequirementCompletionClosure's measured edge count away from 29 for a reason unrelated to this outcome, and narrowing only the application command would make the widest edge in the domain the narrowest edge in the layer above it -- a layer silently contradicting the layer it depends on, which is worse than a documented two-cell gap. Recording rather than asserting follows internal/application/framing_test.go:562-564's stated reason: asserting a defect pins it in place and turns its repair into a failure in a file the repairing task may not own.

decisions.decision: Authority is owner-ONLY for all three verbs, and this is a measurement twice over rather than a preference. (i) The product names the actor and never names another: user-facing-spec.md:274 '人間の指示で新しい処理を停止している', :277 '人間が以後の処理を取り消した', domain-model.md:269 '人間が処理を停止', :273 '人間が以後の解決を不要と判断', :211 '人間が発行した...command', and user-facing-spec.md:191-201 puts the triple under '利用者は...次を実行できる'. Not one of these names the Loop, the scheduler or a Runner. (ii) application.Role (internal/application/caller.go:11-16) declares exactly THREE values -- RoleOwner, RoleRunner, RoleScheduler (measured: `grep -c 'Role = "' internal/application/caller.go` returns 3) -- and internal/api/auth.go PRODUCES exactly two of them, at auth.go:50 and :85 (RoleRunner) and auth.go:59 and :99 (RoleOwner). RoleScheduler is produced by no non-test line in the repository; every non-test occurrence is a role ACCEPTED by a command, never a role a transport constructs. So callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner) is both what the product describes and the only reachable choice, and the two arguments converge instead of trading off. All three commands therefore call callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner) and nothing else, and the HTTP branches gate on caller.Role != application.RoleOwner exactly as the :answer-input branch already does at internal/api/api.go:439-442.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 2 is an authority question and the only way to make it measurable is to enumerate the authority vocabulary and then refuse everything outside the named subset. Role is a closed three-value enum in one file, which makes 'every role the product does not name' a finite, checkable set of exactly two -- RoleRunner and RoleScheduler -- rather than an open-ended promise. Choosing owner+scheduler by copying StartFraming would have been the easy error: StartFraming's own comment (framing.go:80-90) argues for scheduler on the ground that a scheduler-ONLY command would be unreachable, which is an argument for including owner, not an argument for including scheduler. Here the product's own words settle it, and the measured unreachability of RoleScheduler means excluding it costs no reachable behaviour.

decisions.decision: The permit asymmetry, which is the load-bearing safety decision. PAUSE and CANCEL evaluate NO domain.Permit at all and are allowed under all seven control modes. RESUME evaluates domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitClaim and is therefore allowed under exactly TWO of the seven. The rule that produces both, stated once: a permit exists to withhold the Loop's capacity and its side effects, so it must gate an operation that can INCREASE what the Loop may do and must not gate one that can only REDUCE it. Pause and cancel only ever reduce; resume is the only one of the three that restores. Measured consequence from domain.permitAllowed (internal/domain/control.go:266-281): with PermitClaim, allow ALLOWS, pause-intake ALLOWS, pause-claim DENIES, graceful-stop DENIES, immediate-stop DENIES, emergency-stop DENIES, cancel DENIES -- 2 of 7, byte-identical to the table V2-084's CompleteFraming asserts and cross-checkable against internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go:242's permitAllowedTable mirror exactly as internal/application/framing_test.go:340 already does. Nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit by any of the three, because EffectFromPermit (control.go:297-301) requires the current effective mode to be exactly ControlAllow, which would deny resume under pause-intake and -- far worse -- would deny a PAUSE under every non-allow mode.
decisions.rationale: Gating pause behind any permit kind is the single most attractive wrong answer here, because it looks symmetric and it copies a precedent. It is a trap and the measurement shows why: PermitClaim would make pause DENIED under pause-claim, graceful-stop, immediate-stop, emergency-stop and cancel, and PermitIntake would make it DENIED under pause-intake -- in both cases the owner could not stop a Requirement while a stop was already in force, which contradicts definition.md:132 and :137 head-on. An ungated pause is admittedly the same SHAPE as Plan's and Prepare's measured defect (framing_test.go:565's TestPlanAndPrepareAreMeasuredUnderEmergencyStop), and the distinction is not special pleading: Plan and Prepare CREATE an Increment and a canonical target, so they increase what the Loop may do under a stop, while pause and cancel remove. The rule as written discriminates correctly in all four cases with no exceptions. The one property this asymmetry buys is the one the outcome is about: under emergency-stop, resume is denied and cancel is allowed, so a paused Requirement retains at least one exit under every one of the seven modes.

decisions.decision: The single integer that discriminates the right design from both wrong ones: TestInvariant3RequirementCompletionClosure's wantEdgeCount (internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go:730) must remain EXACTLY 29 after this change. Its BFS (invariant_model_test.go:697-726) explores every RequirementCommandKind from every reachable status to fixpoint, building each fixture as `Requirement{ID: "requirement", Status: from, Version: 5}` -- with PausedFrom at its ZERO value. A resume that is gated on PausedFrom being a member of the pausable set is therefore refused in that fixture and contributes ZERO edges: the count stays 29 and wantReachedStatusCount stays 10. A resume that ignores the memory and always restores a fixed status contributes one edge from paused and makes it 30. Four widened existing branches contribute four edges from paused and make it 33. The coordinator computed 29 independently, by hand, from model.go's ten branches -- captured 2, framing 3, ready 4, active 6, waiting 5, needs-input 2, paused 1, recovering 4, evaluating 2, cancelled 0 -- and the sum agreeing with the constant already in the tree is what makes it safe to use as a discriminator. Exactly TWO edits are permitted in this test: wantRequirementCommandCount 9 -> 10 (invariant_model_test.go:665) and one entry appended to allRequirementCommandKinds (:656-660). The BFS fixture line and both want constants at :729-730 stay byte-unchanged. 30 or 33 is a stop-and-escalate.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 3 needed to be measurable rather than promised, and a hand-written round-trip test is not enough on its own: it proves the paths it walks and says nothing about the paths it forgot. An exhaustive fixpoint search over a finite labelled transition system already exists in this repository, already produces a single integer, and already fails loudly when the integer moves -- and by a genuine accident of its fixture it is blind to a correctly-gated resume and loud about both incorrect ones. Using it means the guard against resuming into a state the Requirement was never in is enforced by a test the implementer must open anyway to widen the command axis, in the same edit, with no new machinery.

decisions.decision: What Validate may and may not demand, decided by asking which record would be trapped. Validate's Requirement case (model.go:317-336) gains exactly ONE clause, modelled on the RequestedBy clause three lines above it: if PausedFrom is non-empty it must be a member of the pausable set, otherwise the record is rejected as unreadable. Validate does NOT gain the converse demand: a Requirement whose Status is paused and whose PausedFrom is empty stays VALID. The reason is the trap. DecideRequirement calls Validate on its first line (model.go:456-458), so any record Validate rejects is a record no command can be issued against -- including cancel. A paused record with no remembered origin is precisely the record that most needs an exit, so making it invalid would recreate the trap this task exists to remove, one level down. RequirementResume refuses it with ErrInvalidTransition; RequirementCancel still succeeds. The asymmetry with the completed clause immediately above (model.go:324-328, where a completed Requirement without a StableSnapshot IS invalid) is justified by terminality and must be written into the code comment: an invalid completed record needs no exit because completed is terminal, while paused is the one non-terminal status whose entire design problem is having one.
decisions.rationale: This is the decision a mechanical implementation gets wrong by being tidy. Symmetry with the completed clause is superficially attractive and would produce an aggregate that cannot be rescued, which is a strictly worse failure than the one the task was created to fix -- a record that is not merely trapped in a status but unreadable by every code path. The clause that IS added is the safe half: garbage in PausedFrom has no legitimate reading, cannot arise from any branch this design writes, and is caught by d7's and d10's tests long before it could be persisted, so rejecting it costs nothing real. The trade-off is recorded rather than hidden, because a reviewer must be able to see that it was decided.

decisions.decision: Three application commands in ONE new file, internal/application/pause.go, each following StartFraming's discipline line for line, and internal/application/service.go is NOT edited. Service.PauseRequirement, Service.ResumeRequirement and Service.CancelRequirement each: callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner); requireRequest(req.RequestID); requestFingerprint with its own verb string; s.mutate with its own idempotency scope, the ErrIdempotencyConflict refusal on a same-key different-fingerprint replay, and restoreResponse; read the Requirement or ErrNotFound; take the instant from transactionAuthorityTime(ctx, u); call domain.DecideRequirement with the caller's actor and the request's ExpectedVersion; u.SaveRequirement(ctx, next, r.Version); and s.record with a nil OutboxItem. Resume additionally resolves the ControlTarget from u.RequirementRepositoryLink and the revision from domain.EffectiveControl INSIDE the transaction and evaluates domain.Permit with PermitClaim, exactly as framing.go:160-183 does. Event types: requirement.paused, requirement.resumed, requirement.cancelled -- measured to need no schema change, because contracts/schemas/domain-event.json:4 constrains event_type by the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{1,63}$ and by no enum. No request carries a control_revision, a repository_id or a timestamp. No new port: internal/application/ports.go is prohibited.
decisions.rationale: A new file rather than an addition to framing.go or service.go is a conflict decision as much as a structural one: internal/application/service.go is held by V2-083 and V2-085 and internal/application/framing.go and framing_test.go by V2-084 and V2-085, and every helper these three commands need -- s.mutate, requireRequest, requestFingerprint, restoreResponse, transactionAuthorityTime, s.record -- is package-private and callable from a sibling file without touching either. Naming the file pause.go rather than lifecycle.go is deliberate: its subject is the paused status and its two exits, and cancel belongs in it because cancel IS one of the two exits. Separating the trap from its escape across two files is how the exit becomes a follow-up again.

decisions.decision: What is measured, in three grades, each labelled with what it cannot reach. GRADE 1, internal/domain, pure and exhaustive, in a new file internal/domain/pause_resume_test.go: for all 11 statuses x the 4 pausable PausedFrom values and the empty value (55 cells), resume succeeds if and only if Status is paused AND PausedFrom is a member of the pausable set, and on success next.Status EQUALS PausedFrom exactly and next.PausedFrom is empty; the round trip for all FOUR pausable statuses, asserting the same Status returns, Version incremented by exactly 2, PausedFrom cleared, and every other field unchanged via the extended requirementsEqual; a second pause is refused from paused and leaves PausedFrom byte-unchanged, for all four; both exits available from all four; and a paused record with an empty PausedFrom is Validate-valid, resume-refused and cancel-accepted. GRADE 2, internal/application, over the real Service and a real store, in a new file internal/application/pause_test.go: the same round trip for all four pausable statuses by SEEDING the store, plus the seven-mode tables, plus the refusal matrix. GRADE 3, over the composed HTTP handler in internal/api/api_test.go and against the real binary and the real Firestore emulator in internal/api/live_local_test.go: the round trip for ready and active ONLY. The reason grade 3 stops at two of four is measured, not assumed: domain.RequirementWait and domain.RequirementRecover still have no non-test issuer, so no journey can put a Requirement into waiting or recovering. State that as a limit of this task, never as a gap in the assertion.
decisions.rationale: The three grades exist because the honest answer to 'is the round trip proved' is different at each altitude, and collapsing them would either overclaim or undertest. Grade 1 is the only place all four transitions can be proved, and it can prove them exhaustively because DecideRequirement is a pure function -- 55 cells cost nothing and a sample would leave exactly the forgotten cell where the bug lives. Grade 2 can still reach all four by seeding, which is worth doing because it proves the application layer carries the field through the store rather than dropping it. Grade 3 genuinely cannot reach two of the four, and V2-084's A12 set the precedent for naming that boundary in the evidence instead of quietly testing something weaker. The implementer must re-measure the two unissued commands rather than trust this sentence.

decisions.decision: The other half of a pause already exists and this task must MEASURE the composition rather than describe it. docs/architecture/domain-model.md:295 states the product's own decomposition: pausing is expressed as the combination of a Control Intent whose scope includes the Increment and the parent Requirement's Status transition to paused. The Control Intent half is already shipped and already reachable -- POST /v1/controls (contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml:55-64) writes a domain.ControlIntent through Service.Control (internal/application/service.go:1307) and that function never touches a Requirement's Status. And the propagation is real, not aspirational, by a measurement worth stating: Service.Plan writes the canonical ControlTarget with InstallationID, RepositoryID, IncrementID AND RequirementID (service.go:963-966), and Service.Claim reads that same canonical target back through u.CanonicalTarget and evaluates domain.Permit against it (service.go:1207-1232), so a Control Intent with Scope{Kind: requirement} and Mode cancel MATCHES a claim of that Requirement's Increment (domain.matches, control.go:138-139) and DENIES it (permitAllowed(cancel, PermitClaim) is false). The implementer must execute exactly that: set a requirement-scoped cancel Intent, then attempt to claim a planned and prepared Increment of that Requirement, and assert domain.ErrControlDenied. What this task does NOT do is fuse the two halves: Service.PauseRequirement writes no Control Intent and Service.Control transitions no Requirement.
decisions.rationale: V2-084's A13(ii) deferred cancel because 'what a Control Intent with mode cancel scoped to a Requirement does to that Requirement' was an open control-plane question. It is now answered by measurement: it does nothing to the Requirement's status and it denies every gated operation on it, so the two halves are complementary and neither subsumes the other. Fusing them was the tempting move and it is wrong three times over -- user-facing-spec.md:288-296 forbids synchronising two lifecycles into one state; one request_id would own two idempotency stories, which is the argument framing.go:48-50 already makes against a flag on CaptureRequest; and the Control Intent carries the acknowledgment and verification lifecycle (domain-model.md:216) that definition.md:164 requires before a stop may be called complete, which a Requirement status transition has none of. Executing the composition instead of asserting it is what stops the openapi text from being the only evidence that the owner's full path exists.

decisions.decision: The three routes, and one additive read field so the exit survives a closed browser tab. internal/api/api.go gains POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:pause, :resume and :cancel in the POST default branch, by the same prefix-plus-suffix idiom, with three named suffix constants beside startFramingSuffix (api.go:604-610), each gated to RoleOwner. Collision-freedom is measured, not assumed: the only HasSuffix branches in the file are at api.go:401 (/v1/leases/ :renew), :406 (/v1/executions/ :start), :416, :434 and :454, no existing suffix under requirementsPrefix is a suffix of any new one or vice versa, and the GET /v1/requirements/ branches at :176 and :319 are method-gated. Response shapes: PauseResponse carries requirement_id, status and version PLUS resumes_to, the status a resume would restore; ResumeResponse and CancelResponse carry the three. And RequirementDetailResponse gains ONE optional field, resumes_to, omitted entirely unless the status is paused -- the same 'omitted entirely' discipline repository_id and captured_at already use at openapi:483. That is the only edit permitted in internal/application/readmodels.go.
decisions.rationale: resumes_to is not decoration; it is the difference between an exit that exists and an exit the owner can find. A way out visible only in the response to the pause is still a trap for anyone who closed the tab, and the detail route is where an owner returning the next day actually looks. It also makes the round trip assertable in the API's own vocabulary in one line: the resumes_to in the pause response equals the status before the pause and equals the status in the resume response. The field is additive and optional, so no existing response moves. What readmodels.go must NOT gain is a paused branch in nextAction (readmodels.go:309-332, measured to branch on completed and cancelled and on Increment and Execution status and never on paused, so a paused Requirement with a running Execution reports 'monitor execution'): that string is a claim about what to do next, and until a pause propagates to the Runner -- which this task does not deliver -- changing it would assert a stop completion that definition.md:164 says has not been observed. Measure that gap and log it as a finding; do not fix it and do not assert it.

decisions.decision: The closed-set guards this change must move, and the ones it must not. MUST move, and each is a mandatory edit rather than a nuisance: capture_time_test.go:250's want list of Requirement's fields, from seven names to eight, in struct order, with no tag; capture_time_test.go:94-116's startStatusFor table, which fails outright on a kind with no declared start status, gains `case RequirementResume: return RequirementPaused`; capture_time_test.go:47-60's requirementWithStatus must set PausedFrom when the status is paused, exactly as it already sets StableSnapshot when the status is completed, or TestCapturedAtSurvivesEveryRequirementCommandKind fails at :140 on a refused transition; invariant_model_test.go:665's wantRequirementCommandCount 9 -> 10 and :656-660's kind list; and invariant_model_test.go:673-687's requirementsEqual must compare PausedFrom, or every 'mutated a rejected requirement' assertion in the package goes blind to the one field this task's new code writes. MUST NOT move: internal/domain/source_guard_test.go, which is PROHIBITED -- this design adds no import to internal/domain in any file, production or test, so nonTestImportAllowlist (source_guard_test.go:253-260, five entries) and testImportAllowlist (:265-276, ten entries, containing neither reflect nor encoding/json) both stay byte-unchanged; and internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go, also prohibited, whose wantStopMatrixCells is 56 over eight named operations with a total of 12 allowed cells that docs/product/definition.md:156-159 cites by name.
decisions.rationale: Every one of these is a guard that will fail loudly if it is not updated and will silently under-measure if it is updated carelessly, and requirementsEqual is the dangerous one: the package's rejection assertions all run through it, so an implementer who adds the field and not the comparison ships a test suite that cannot see a resume mutating the memory on a command it refused. Prohibiting source_guard_test.go is the surprising choice and it is deliberate: it converts 'this design needs no new dependency' from a claim into a build failure, because the only way to import reflect or encoding/json in internal/domain is to widen an allowlist in a file this task may not open. Prohibiting stop_matrix_test.go is the same move for a different reason -- enrolling three new operations in that matrix would change a count docs/product/definition.md cites and would drag docs/** into a task whose whole point is that the documents already say enough.

decisions.decision: Quota, re-measured, with V2-084's own constraint found STALE. V2-084's A15 and its constraints state that the in-memory adapter does not call quota.Counter.TrueUp and that therefore only FOUR read transactions fit in one budget day. At bcca4a0 that is no longer true: V2-087 landed the correction, and internal/store/memory/store.go:353 now calls u.s.quota.TrueUp(u.quotaKey, u.quotaReserved, actual) under a section header naming V2-087 at store.go:178-188 and :344-353. The arithmetic V2-084 relied on is still readable -- quota.DefaultBudget is {Reads: 25000, Writes: 10000, Deletes: 10000} at internal/quota/quota.go:46 and quota.ReadTransactionUsage is {Reads: 6001, Writes: 1} at quota.go:56, which is 4 read transactions before the true-up existed -- but the adapter now charges actual reads. Do not copy either number. Re-measure the wall by execution, report both values, and still measure each of the three new mutation paths against quota.MutationUsage {Reads: 32, Writes: 16} (quota.go:63): that reservation is applied BEFORE the callback can stage anything, so a transaction whose real reads exceed 32 fails regardless of true-up. If a read budget still binds the HTTP journey, advance the injected clock between detail reads; do not weaken an assertion, drop a read, merge two assertions into one read or raise a budget.
decisions.rationale: This is the concrete illustration of why every number in a packet is expected to be stale, and it is worth writing out rather than gesturing at: the single most operationally load-bearing constraint in the packet this task depends on was invalidated by the task that landed immediately before it. An implementer who inherited V2-084's sentence would have contorted a test around a wall that is gone. The MutationUsage half survives the change and is the half that can still fail, which is why it is separated out and still required.

decisions.decision: Rollback, stated as a property with the one surviving artefact named. Reverting means deleting internal/application/pause.go, internal/application/pause_test.go and internal/domain/pause_resume_test.go, and undoing: one field on domain.Requirement, one RequirementCommandKind, one switch case, one pausable-set helper, two assignments in the pause branch, one Validate clause, five edits in two internal/domain test files, three routes plus three suffix constants plus three handlers plus three body types in internal/api/api.go, one field on the requirement detail read model, three path blocks and six schema blocks in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, and the new tests in internal/api. Nothing else must be undone: this change adds no port, no document kind, no index, no collection, no environment variable, no outbox item, no event kind outside the existing pattern, and no import edge in any of the four components. The one artefact that survives a revert is a stored Requirement whose document carries a PausedFrom key the reverted code does not know: json.Unmarshal ignores an unknown key, so such a record reads back as a paused Requirement with no memory -- which d8 deliberately made a VALID, cancellable, non-resumable record. Verify that claim by measurement: after a revert, a Requirement stored in paused still reads through GET /v1/requirements/{id} and through the export without error.
decisions.rationale: The honest form of a rollback story is to enumerate what could survive and show that each item is inert, and here exactly one thing survives. It is inert only because of the Validate decision in d8, which makes the rollback argument and the trap argument the same argument -- the reason a paused record with no memory must stay valid is not only that it needs an exit today but that a revert can manufacture one tomorrow. Stating it this way also gives the coordinator a real answer to 'can this be reverted', rather than a claim that no state was written.

decisions.decision: Chain position and the manifest, stated as facts. Components: domain, application, api, contracts -- four evidence records and exactly four evidence keys. This task creates and removes NO component edge: internal/domain gains a field, a constant, a switch case and an unexported helper using only symbols and imports the package already has (ci/components.json declares domain's dependencies as the empty list, measured); internal/application gains a file using only domain plus what the package already imports; internal/api gains branches, handlers and body types; and no test-only import is new. Because no edge moves, a red manifest, dependency-coverage or key-closure check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate rather than editing ci/components.json, which is prohibited and which would additionally move all 23 evidence keys because ci/** is in all_on_change. Ordering: this task must be serialized AFTER V2-084, which lands the ready and start edges, POST :complete-framing and the openapi path this task's three paths sit beside, and which also holds internal/api/api.go, internal/api/api_test.go, internal/api/live_local_test.go and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml -- a four-file conflict. Editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml (1044 lines and 25 declared /v1 paths at bcca4a0, measured) moves the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest and enrols this task in the api-contract chain.
decisions.rationale: The coordinator needs the conflict set and the edge answer, and the edge answer here is unusually clean: this is a task that edits internal/domain -- the component with an empty dependency list and the strictest import allowlist in the repository -- and adds nothing to it but a field, a constant and a branch. That is the strongest available evidence that the state machine was extended by exactly one edge rather than opened up, and it is why the manifest checks can be treated as a stopping condition rather than a chore.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api
risks: The single largest risk is a resume that lands somewhere legal instead of somewhere remembered. It passes a casual round-trip test written from ready, because ready happens to be a legal target from paused under every wrong design. The guard is TestInvariant3RequirementCompletionClosure's wantEdgeCount staying exactly 29 (internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go:730) plus the 55-cell exhaustive table in grade 1: 30 means resume ignored the memory, 33 means four existing branches were widened. Either is a stop-and-escalate, not a constant to adjust.

A second pause overwriting the memory is the most destructive single bug available here: it would set PausedFrom to paused and make the Requirement unresumable while looking successful. The domain already prevents it, because paused is not in the pause branch's admitted source set (internal/domain/model.go:511), but that protection is invisible unless it is asserted. Assert that a second pause with a different request_id is refused AND that PausedFrom is byte-unchanged afterwards, for all four pausable statuses.

Gating pause or cancel behind any domain.Permit turns the feature into the defect. Under PermitClaim a pause would be denied by pause-claim, graceful-stop, immediate-stop, emergency-stop and cancel; under PermitIntake by pause-intake; and routing either through domain.EffectFromPermit would deny it under all six non-allow modes at once. An owner who cannot stop a Requirement while a stop is in force contradicts docs/product/definition.md:132 and :137. Only resume evaluates a Permit.

internal/domain/capture_time_test.go's requirementWithStatus (line 47) will make TestCapturedAtSurvivesEveryRequirementCommandKind fail as soon as RequirementResume joins the kind axis, because the fixture leaves PausedFrom empty and resume refuses it. The correct fix is to have the fixture set PausedFrom for a paused status, exactly as it already sets StableSnapshot for a completed one. The wrong fix -- making resume tolerate an empty memory -- is the wantEdgeCount = 30 defect wearing a different hat.

requirementsEqual (internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go:673) compares Requirement field by field and has no reflect import available to save it. If PausedFrom is not added to that comparison, every 'mutated a rejected requirement' assertion in internal/domain goes blind to the one field this task's new code writes, and the package keeps passing while measuring less than it did before.

internal/api/api.go, internal/api/api_test.go, internal/api/live_local_test.go and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml are all held by V2-084, which must land first and which this task builds directly on. Running the two concurrently conflicts in four files, and running this one first would leave it with no ready and no active status to pause.

V2-084's quota constraint is stale at bcca4a0: V2-087 added the in-memory true-up at internal/store/memory/store.go:353, so the four-read-transactions-per-day wall it describes is gone. An implementer who plans around the stale wall will contort the HTTP journey for no reason; one who ignores quota entirely may still exceed quota.MutationUsage's 32 reads in a single new mutation, which the pre-callback reservation fails on regardless of true-up. Re-measure both.

The read model is where an honest pause quietly becomes a dishonest one. nextAction (internal/application/readmodels.go:309) has no paused branch, so a paused Requirement with a running Execution reports 'monitor execution'. Fixing that string would assert a stop completion that docs/product/definition.md:164 says requires observing worker ack, process exit and lease release -- none of which this task delivers. Measure it, log it as a finding for the tech_lead, and change only the additive resumes_to field.
